description: The Settings window (desktop refinement §14.1). It is granted the SAME application-command permission as the control window, and that is a deliberate decision rather than convenience: Settings is where the speech model is downloaded and verified, where displays are listed and identified, where the optical rigs are calibrated, where a backup is exported or restored, and where the support bundle is written. Narrowing the grant would mean maintaining a second list that has to be widened every time a setting gains a backing command — and a list that is wrong in the closed direction fails as a broken screen, which is the kind of failure people work around by widening it in a hurry. What this does NOT mean is that the window is bounded by having no library, editor or session UI: `allow-control-commands` includes listing and deleting scripts and starting and ending sessions, and a compromised renderer invokes commands directly rather than through buttons. The grant is as wide as control's, and it is accepted as such. What is genuinely withheld is what is withheld from control too — `opener:default` and the dialog plugin — so no window in this application can choose a filesystem path; every picker runs in Rust (§50.7). Its CORE grant, on the other hand, is not the same as control's: event listen and unlisten, for every subscription and its teardown, and `core:window:allow-current-monitor`, which the calibration wizard uses to tell whether it is about to cover this window's own panel. It emits nothing — opening a Settings section is broadcast from control — and the rest of `core:default` (the menu builder with `set_as_app_menu`, tray icons, image, path, resources, app, webview, and the rest of the window plugin) is withheld for the same reasons control.json gives (#267). The argument above for one shared list does not carry over: a core call is an `@tauri-apps/api` import, so the frontend's use of them is a short list that can be read off the code, and tests/acl_tests.rs names every allowed one. The wizard's monitor read fails open, so losing that grant would not break a screen — it would silently switch the guard off, and the test is what notices. The window plugin's `start_dragging` and `internal_toggle_maximize` are granted for the same reason as the control window's: on a Mac the titlebar is an overlay, and Tauri's drag script moves the window by its toolbar band. Both commands accept another window's label; the drag script never passes one, and the most either can do is move or zoom a window.
